title: Big's Backyard Ultra — Wikipedia article (history, past results, day/night course)
claims: The event is the original backyard ultra, invented by Gary "Lazarus Lake" Cantrell of Bell Buckle, Tennessee, and inaugurated in 2011.
Participants run a 4.167-mile loop every hour and are eliminated if they fail to complete a loop within the hour; the loop runs on trails during the day and along a road after dark.

Each loop equals 100 miles divided by 24, so a runner who completes a full day of 24 loops covers 100 miles; there is no predefined finish, and the winner completes one loop no other competitor completes.

Compiled past winners and laps: 2011 Tim Englund 18 (assist Dave Carver); 2012 Joe Fejes 28 (Marcy Beard); 2013 Tim Englund 35 (Keith Knipling); 2014 no winner at 49 laps (Johan Steene / Jeremy Ebel); 2016 Babak Rastgoufard 29 (Andy Pearson); 2017 Guillaume Calmettes 59 (Harvey Lewis); 2018 Johan Steene 68 (Courtney Dauwalter); 2019 Maggie Guterl 60 (William Hayward, first female winner); 2021 Harvey Lewis 85 (Chris Roberts); 2022 Piotr Chadovich 76 (Harvey Lewis); 2023 Harvey Lewis 108 (Ihor Verys); 2024 Scott Snell 88 (Megan Eckert); 2025 Phil Gore 114 (Ivo Steyaert).
In 2020 the COVID-19 pandemic precluded international travel to Tennessee; the race was replaced by satellite events and the world title was won by Karel Sabbe in Belgium with 76 laps.
